name: Naval Aircraft Factory N3N Canary
summary: The US Navy's last biplane trainer, 'Yellow Peril', a Naval Aircraft Factory design flown as landplane and floatplane until 1961 and now a favorite of private warbird owners.

wings: Biplane with a single bay of struts on each side
Upper and lower wings of similar size with rounded tips
engines: Wright Whirlwind radial in a smooth round cowl
fuselage: Often a bright overall yellow finish
Fixed conventional gear (or a central float with outer wing floats on the seaplane)

tellTales: Open-cockpit biplane in overall bright yellow with a round radial nose
Single-bay biplane with a squat, rounded fuselage
Round cowl, squarish tail and a squat, short-coupled body

confusedWith.howToTell: The Stearman has longer, more angular lines and a larger, rougher radial; the N3N is squatter with a smooth round cowl and a stubby fuselage.
The Ryan is a monoplane; the N3N is a biplane.
The Tiger Moth has an inline engine and a long, slim fuselage with a pointed nose; the N3N has a fat radial nose.
